subject: Request to shift demo & schedule technical dry-run (prep checklist included)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed demo timing + prep checklist for Redwood trial

Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call yesterday. Per our discussion, we'd like to lock a 60-minute product demo the week of Sep 20 and also schedule a 45–60 minute technical dry-run for your engineering team the day prior so we can validate data access and run a couple of prompt traces.

High-level ask: is there a one-hour slot that works for the demo (we'll tailor to your timezone) and a separate 45–60 minute prep window 24 hours before the demo for sample-data ingest and prompt validation?

Prep checklist (what we'll cover during the dry-run):
- Confirm sample data ingest and verify schema (we'll need S3/GCS credentials or a secure upload)
- Run prompt set v3 (attached) against a small workload trace to validate latency/cost expectations
- Validate runbook steps for failover and token limits
- Confirm who will join from your side (engineer + product/PO recommended)

I've attached a quick sample_data_manifest.csv that lists the files we'd like to test with. If you can share preferred slots and the contact for someone who can grant temporary read access, we can get the dry-run on the calendar.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
sean.g@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0119
Redwood Inference

Attachments: sample_data_manifest.csv (CSV, 32KB)
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finlytics.com; Dana Lee <dana.lee@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed demo timing + prep checklist for Redwood trial

Sean —

Appreciate the checklist. Heads up: our VP of Product (who wanted to join) is traveling the week of Sep 20 and we need to shift the demo out a week. Availability for key stakeholders looks best in the week of Sep 27.

For the dry-run, we still want the earlier prep window — ideally the day before the demo — but could we do the technical dry-run the morning of Sep 26 and slot the customer-facing demo on Sep 27 afternoon? That helps us get the sample ingest validated before the exec demo.

Procurement (cc'd) will also need SOC 2 in-scope docs and a short note on data retention for the POC. Can you send a pointer to those resources?

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director of Product, Finlytics
alex.j@finlytics.com | +1 (646) 333-2244

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed demo timing + prep checklist for Redwood trial

Alex —

Thanks — Sep 26 morning dry-run + Sep 27 afternoon demo works on our side. I'll tentatively block both and send calendar invites after we confirm exact times (timezone sanity-check: are you PT or ET?).

Quick answers for procurement: see the links below for SOC 2 summary and our standard POC data-retention policy. I'll also include a short runbook for the dry-run.

Useful links:
- SOC 2 summary: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3PrepDocs (see "SOC2_summary.pdf")
- POC data retention: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/finlytics/deal/FIN-2026-0423 (retention notes in the POC playbook)

I've attached prompt_set_v3.jsonl and a short runbook extract; during the dry-run we'll do a low-volume run of the prompt set and capture latency traces. Can procurement confirm the preferred path for sharing the test data (S3 role vs secure upload)?

Thanks — I'll loop in Marissa to run the dry-run.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt_set_v3.jsonl (JSONL, 14KB); runbook_dryrun_minutes.pdf (PDF, 48KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.c@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finlytics.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.g@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed demo timing + prep checklist for Redwood trial

Alex / Sean —

Looping in as the SE who will run the dry-run. Thanks for that availability. Proposal:
- Dry-run (technical): Sep 26 09:30–10:15 PT — 45 minutes (engineer + data contact)
- Exec demo: Sep 27 14:00–15:00 PT — 60 minutes (product + execs)

Pre-reqs for the dry-run (please confirm before Sep 24):
1) Temporary read-only S3 role OR secure upload link for the sample files listed in sample_data_manifest.csv
2) One engineer with SSH/key access to the test bucket or someone to share files via secure upload
3) A list of 4–6 representative queries/use-cases you want us to run from prompt_set_v3.jsonl

We will:
- Validate schema and ingest a small batch (we'll keep it under 500 records)
- Run prompt set v3 against a trace and capture latency and token-cost estimates
- Walk through the runbook steps for monitoring and failover

If procurement needs anything else before the POC, Sean, can you confirm the SOC 2 pointer and a one-paragraph summary for the procurement mailbox?

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.c@redwood.com | +1 (617) 555-0198

Marissa / Sean —

Thanks — that schedule works. Confirming:
- Dry-run: Sep 26 09:30–10:15 PT (we'll have our data engineer, Priya, on the call)
- Exec demo: Sep 27 14:00–15:00 PT (VP of Product will join)

Procurement: we'll use a temporary S3 role (I'll have Priya create it; she'll email credentials to sean.g@redwood.com and marissa.c@redwood.com by EOD Sep 24). SOC2 summary link looks good; procurement, let us know if you need a standard SLA addendum for the POC.

Marissa — for the 4–6 representative queries, we'll pick ones from the "risk_extraction" and "summary_batch" groups in the prompt set.

Looking forward — I'll accept the invites when they come through.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Director of Product | Finlytics
